steps.name: Anat
steps.text: Ugh...
Anat! You're awake?

steps.name: Anat
steps.text: *Gasp* My head hurts...

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: You hit your head when you fainted. That's probably why.

steps.name: Anat
steps.text: It's not just my head. I'm aching all over. Why is there a bruise on my shoulder?

steps.name: Anat
steps.text: And my knee?

steps.name: Nameless Mummy
steps.text: Ugh...

steps.name: Anat
steps.text: Eek! Get away from me!

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: Calm down, Anat! Calm down.

steps.name: Anat
steps.text: How am I supposed to calm down when a corpse just came back to life? It touched my ears, didn't it? Do I still have my ears?

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: It's just copying other people's movements. It doesn't mean any harm, to you or anyone else.

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: Just treat it as a piece of moving furniture!

steps.name: Nameless Mummy
steps.text: Ugh...

steps.name: Anat
steps.text: Why do you seem so comfortable with this, Pepe?

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: Don't look at me like that, please!

steps.name: Anat
steps.text: What did you do?

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: Yesterday... I placed a gem that I dug up into its chest. The Originium circuit engraved into the gem woke it up.

steps.name: Anat
steps.text: Yesterday?

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: You wouldn't loan me an important archaeological discovery like this. The Varjavandabad Museum holds respect from the Shahanshah. Not even a shahzada like me could pull rank here.

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: So... I had to sneak in.

steps.name: Anat
steps.text: There's a reason I didn't want to lend it to you, Pepe.

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: What is it? If you're worried about co-authorship, I'm cool.

steps.name: Anat
steps.text: It's not that...

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: Investment? Sponsorship? I'll renovate your entire museum, if you want!

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: Why are you looking at me like that?

steps.name: Anat
steps.text: I don't understand... why are you so obsessed with becoming the Historian of Shar-Agade? You can still carry on your research if you agree to inherit the title of Padishah from your father.

steps.name: Anat
steps.text: But once you become an historian and enter the City of Gold, you will never be allowed to leave. You know that.

steps.name: Anat
steps.text: All that you learned in school, all the training you underwent to hunt ruins in the desert, all that you've seen on your journeys, all that will become useless if you're the Shahanshah's historian.

steps.name: Anat
steps.text: Are you simply not happy with the fact that your brother was chosen?

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: My dream of becoming the court historian isn't some whim. It's the dream of everyone in my family.

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: We grew up dreaming about inheriting the golden reed pen from our elders.

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: They tell you that whoever holds the pen carries great responsibility, to record all that has ever happened for posterity.

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: You are writing the truth of your time, the most complete truth that can be known, which needs no conjecture or investigation and can never be buried by sand and earth.

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: That is what I've always wanted to do.

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: I want to tell Sargon's history! I want the glory of the Shah to shine forever by my hand, and to inspire everyone who reads it.

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: Thousands of years later, someone I will never meet will pick up those pages and feel a connection to me and the Shah, linking the three of us.

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: Don't you think that's really romantic, Anat?

steps.name: Anat
steps.text: *Sigh*...

steps.name: Anat
steps.text: I should have known that you wouldn't give up so easily...

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: Shouldn't you and Titi have gotten used to my stubbornness by now?

steps.name: Anat
steps.text: Very well, on behalf of the museum, I approve the loan of the artifact... plus another gem.

steps.name: Anat
steps.text: It was gifted to the museum by a private collector many years ago. We discovered that it was connected to the mummy, but we have no idea how to use it.

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: There's a gem at the museum too?!

steps.name: Anat
steps.text: That's not the point. The point is I'm allowing you to access it.

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: You're going to hand it over so easily?

steps.name: Anat
steps.text: I never said anything about easy. Co-authorship, investment, sponsorship, plus naming rights fees for the new exhibition hall.

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: Absolutely! With pleasure!

steps.name: Anat
steps.text: Pepe...

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: Yes?

steps.name: Anat
steps.text: Things don't always turn out the way we expect them to. I hope you understand this before you start your investigation.
Anat opens the drawer and takes out a wrapped package.
She unwraps it to reveal a pyramid-shaped gem, identical to the one that was placed in the mummy's chest.
Pepe takes the gem, holding back the urge to cry out in joy.

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: 'Second, the lungs. At their first breath, we come to feel.'

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: Don't let me down.
Pepe reaches into the mummy's chest cavity. The gem is absorbed by the blue light inside as soon as it approaches.

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: Guardian, sealed in sand, I hereby return to you the memories lost to time.

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: Show the path to the Shah's trove, traveler from the past!

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: It stopped moving after I put in the second gem?

steps.name: Anat
steps.text: Did... you expect something different?
Eek—!!

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: That wasn't me. Who's screaming?

steps.name: Anat
steps.text: It was Titi's voice.

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: Is something happening?

steps.name: Anat
steps.text: I'll investigate. Keep an eye on the exhibit.

steps.name: Medjehtiqedti
steps.text: Why didn't you tell me you were just an ordinary cloudbeast?

steps.name: Medjehtiqedti
steps.text: Well... I guess ordinary cloudbeasts don't understand human speech.

steps.name: Medjehtiqedti
steps.text: Looks like all the visitors have been evacuated. It's safe for us to go out now. Do you think you could find your way back to Lazvar if I put you down outside?

steps.name: Medjehtiqedti
steps.text: Hey, stop hitting me! I'm carrying you so you don't have to walk yourself!

steps.name: Medjehtiqedti
steps.text: That's right. Awww, such nice fur... come, I'll introduce you to other little friends of yours.

steps.name: Medjehtiqedti
steps.text: Look at the imagery on this powder box. This cloudbeast is depicted in equal prominence to a high official. I restored this, by the way.

steps.name: Medjehtiqedti
steps.text: And here. This mural is a rare treasure that came from Shar-Agade, the City of Gold.

steps.name: Medjehtiqedti
steps.text: In order to accurately restore it, I looked through every book I could find on the Golden City, and even interviewed people who have been there.

steps.name: Medjehtiqedti
steps.text: Wait. Does that make me sound like I'm after the secrets of Shar-Agade?

steps.name: Medjehtiqedti
steps.text: Shouldn't think too much about it. You're just a cloudbeast, and there's no one else in the museum. It's not like what I just said would get me in trouble.
Suddenly, she hears the faint sound of cracking.

steps.name: Medjehtiqedti
steps.text: Don't tell me...

steps.name: Medjehtiqedti
steps.text: No—! Why did the glass have to pick now to crack?

spans.text: No—! Why did the glass have to pick

steps.name: Medjehtiqedti
steps.text: I'm dead if Anat finds out!
Medjehtiqedti runs toward the display stand, and is shocked by the sight of broken glass littering the floor.
Display cases use specially tempered glass. In the controlled environment of the museum, an accident like this should not have been possible.
She looks up to check on the exhibit, but finds the case empty under the pale light.
She feels a cold, sharp object pressing against her back as she attempts to examine the broken glass.

steps.name: Medjehtiqedti
steps.text: If this is some kind of joke, you can stop.

steps.name: Medjehtiqedti
steps.text: I'm too busy for this.

steps.name: Medjehtiqedti
steps.text: Playing dumb? Which department are you from?

steps.name: Medjehtiqedti
steps.text: I'm going to dock your pay, if you don't start talking...
Medjehtiqedti feels the object pressed against her back move away. She sighs of relief and turns around.

steps.name: Medjehtiqedti
steps.text: One of the interns? You've got nerve, playing practical jokes on the vice curator. I'll let you off easy this time...

steps.name: Medjehtiqedti
steps.text: Eek—!

steps.name: Medjehtiqedti
steps.text: You... you...

steps.name: Medjehtiqedti
steps.text: How did you get out of your case?!

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: Why haven't I heard anything else after that scream? Anat hasn't come back yet... well, I'll just look around.

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: Anat never changes, does she? She's the acting curator, yet her office still looks so bare and sparse.

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: She had so many books back in the dorms. Why aren't there any here?

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: She must be hiding them somewhere...

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: I knew it. A hidden bookshelf in the wall.

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: Hmm... My bookshelf at home is due for renovation... I should ask her to introduce me to the designer.

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: Let's see what you have here... A Study on Tribal Religion in the Southwest, Review of Unearthed Riverside Jewelry...

spans.text: Let's see what you have here...
A Study on Tribal Religion in the Southwest

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: Terra: A Journey, by Dr. E. E. Erikson? The name sounds familiar... that's the Victorian scholar who came to speak at the college, isn't it?

spans.text: by Dr. E. E. Erikson? The name sounds familiar... that's the Victorian scholar who came to speak at the college, isn't it?

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: Lost of labels in here. I didn't know Anat liked his books so much.

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: Let's check the section on Sargonian history...

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: (Finally, she's gone.)

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: (This room sure is luxurious... is that gold thread woven into the cushions on the sofa?)

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: (That's the mummy from the poster. They put it right here in the room? I'll never understand the tastes of rich people.)

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: (There she is... good, she's completely distracted...)

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: (With apologies...)
Narantuya walks up softly and reaches into her pocket, taking out the syringe that she has kept hidden within.
She spent countless days and nights training, even when blisters formed on her feet, in order to be able to walk across a sand dune without leaving any footprints.
Now, she can walk through a crowded market, bells hanging from her neck, without making a single sound.
A Padishah's daughter stands before her. All alone.
When Narantuya raises the syringe, however, a hand suddenly grabs hers and immobilizes it in midair.

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: (A hidden bodyguard?)

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: (You—!)
Narantuya cannot speak.
The mummy laying on the sofa has appeared behind her, grabbing her hand with a steely grip.
Her struggles are futile, and all she can do is watch in terror as the needle approaches her own neck.
The other hand of the mummy is clasped across her mouth, not letting go until the entire contents of the syringe have been injected into Narantuya's veins.
As her consciousness gradually fades, she feels the hand lift her by the collar and hold her outside the window.
One last thought flashes through her mind as she feels her feet dangling in the air.
If only she had more competent subordinates.

steps.name: Nameless Mummy
steps.text: An insect lurking in the dark.

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: What...?

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: What's that sound?

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: Y-You're moving again?

steps.name: Nameless Mummy
steps.text: My mind is no longer clouded. There is clarity. I must communicate my cognition through language.

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: A-Are you alive?

steps.name: Nameless Mummy
steps.text: My life has long passed. What you see is simply a well-preserved vessel.

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: Who are you?

steps.name: Nameless Mummy
steps.text: In times of prosperity, I was His Majesty Lugalszargus Shahanshah's personal guard, defending him from the fires of battle.

steps.name: Nameless Mummy
steps.text: In times of decline, I willingly forsook the sweet release of death for the eternal torment of time, defending His Majesty's trove from invaders, safeguarding the Shahanshah's vow, and awaiting...

steps.name: Nameless Mummy
steps.text: Awaiting the return of the Shahanshah.

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: H-How should I call you?

steps.name: Nameless Mummy
steps.text: My name is Zubayidamu Yanur Ayyusuiz.

steps.name: Nameless Mummy
steps.text: You may call me—Zubayr.

steps.name: Curious Child
steps.text: Mother, what is that lady doing sitting by the pond, staring down at the water?

steps.name: Mother
steps.text: She's dressed in Minoan clothes. The Minoans are said to be great thinkers and debaters.

steps.name: Mother
steps.text: She must be thinking about deep, philosophical questions...

steps.name: Curious Child
steps.text: Philo... what?

steps.name: Curious Child
steps.text: But she looks so pretty, sitting there alone...

steps.name: Museum Security
steps.text: Hanimefendi, the museum is closed.

steps.name: Aspasia
steps.text: I know. I'm waiting for it to reopen.

steps.name: Museum Security
steps.text: Well... I'm afraid there's currently no schedule for reopening.

steps.name: Museum Security
steps.text: According to procedure, the curator must declare the emergency resolved, perform a risk assessment, and report to the stakeholders before a reopening date can be announced.

steps.name: Aspasia
steps.text: I know. One of your colleagues already told me.

steps.name: Aspasia
steps.text: As you can see, I'm waiting.

steps.name: Museum Security
steps.text: You said you left something in the museum?

steps.name: Aspasia
steps.text: Yes.

steps.name: Museum Security
steps.text: Is it very urgent? Could you wait for our staff to look for it? We can contact you once we've found it.

steps.name: Aspasia
steps.text: No, I can't wait.

steps.name: Museum Security
steps.text: How about this... I can unlock the door, and we'll have someone accompany you inside.

steps.name: Aspasia
steps.text: Thank you—

steps.name: Curious Child
steps.text: Mother...

steps.name: Mother
steps.text: What is it?

steps.name: Curious Child
steps.text: Is someone jumping from that window?!
Aspasia looks up at the child's cry and sees a woman falling from high up.
With little time to think or look to the guard opening the door, she dashes over and holds out her arms.
